Accurx integrates around the NHS as an assured IM1 live supplier, using NHS Digital's interoperability standards for primary care and connecting bi-directionally to the GP clinical-system duopoly (EMIS Health, TPP SystmOne) and Vision, plus NHS national services including the Personal Demographics Service (PDS), NHS Single Sign-On, NHS Login, and the NHS App. Accurx is a consumer and integrator of NHS FHIR and IM1 interfaces rather than a publisher of its own public developer API: as of this review it operates no public developer portal, no self-serve REST/FHIR API, and no downloadable OpenAPI or FHIR CapabilityStatement. Third-party and trust integrations are arranged through its partnerships and integration teams under partner agreement.

providers.name: Care GP
providers.description: Care GP is a Sydney-based healthcare technology company (Y Combinator Summer 2026) building a suite of AI agents that automate the administrative and operational work of Australian general practice clinics. Its products include Samantha (medical document allocation that files inbound emails, faxes, and scans), Veronica (24/7 inbound and outbound phone and booking management), and a Billing beta for billing and debt-collection automation. Care GP states it is ISO 27001 certified with onshore Australian data storage, multi-factor authentication, and encryption, and reports serving 400+ clinic operators. As of this enrichment pass the company exposes a customer web application (agent.caregp.com.au) but no public developer portal, API documentation, or OpenAPI definition.

providers.name: Nines
providers.description: Nines was a teleradiology and medical-imaging AI startup founded in 2017 and backed by Accel and 8VC (a $16.5M Series A in 2019), co-founded by CEO David Stavens. It built FDA-cleared AI algorithms — NinesAI Emergent Triage (for intracranial hemorrhage and mass effect) and NinesMeasure (a lung-nodule algorithm) — alongside a live teleradiology practice. On 2022-02-18, Sirona Medical acquired Nines' AI technology, clinical data pipeline, machine-learning engines, and key personnel, folding the FDA-cleared devices into RadOS, Sirona's cloud-native Radiology Operating System (reporter, viewer, PACS, worklist, and platform AI). The nines.com domain now redirects to sironamedical.com. There is no public developer API today; a RadOS "Amplify" SDK (TypeScript/Python, REST + streaming APIs, event subscriptions) is on Sirona's roadmap as an early-access program for design partners.

providers.name: Pillar Biosciences
providers.description: Pillar Biosciences is a Natick, Massachusetts molecular diagnostics company, founded in 2014, that develops targeted next-generation sequencing (NGS) solutions for precision oncology. Its proprietary SLIMamp (Stem-Loop Inhibition Mediated amplification) chemistry enables highly multiplexed, single-tube PCR library preparation from as little as 2.5 ng of DNA, and its oncoReveal panel portfolio covers solid tumour tissue, liquid biopsy, haematologic malignancy, BRCA/HRD/methylation and inherited disease testing, alongside an InheritReveal line and a VersaTile machine-learning panel-design platform. Sequencing data is processed by PiVAT (Pillar Variant Analysis Toolkit), a secondary-analysis pipeline available as a local install or a HIPAA-scoped cloud deployment, with optional OncoKB-powered tertiary reporting. Pillar ships both research-use-only kits and an IVD product line, and raised a $34.5M round led by Illumina in 2025. Pillar publishes no public API, SDK or developer program; PiVAT's integration surface is bioinformatics file formats (FASTQ, BAM, VCF, PDF) behind a customer login.

providers.name: Sage Care
providers.description: Sage Care (sagecare.ai) builds an AI-native, HIPAA-compliant software platform made exclusively for home care agencies. Its product bundles an AI receptionist, a purpose-built CRM, an AI notetaker and a clinical scribe that automate the intake, referral, scheduling and documentation work that home care operators handle every day. Sage Care integrates with existing home care management systems such as WellSky and AxisCare rather than replacing them, and ships native iOS and desktop applications for caregivers and office staff. The company is backed by General Catalyst and surfaced through its portfolio. As of this enrichment pass Sage Care publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDKs, or developer documentation — it is an application vendor rather than an API provider, so this profile captures company identity and security/compliance posture only.

providers.name: Swift Medical
providers.description: Swift Medical develops AI-powered wound and skin care management software for healthcare organizations across acute, post-acute, home health, and hospice settings. Its flagship Skin & Wound app captures calibrated wound images on mobile devices, applies computer-vision tissue analytics and auto-tracing to measure and classify wounds, and coordinates care through longitudinal documentation backed by the company's database of more than 32 million wound images. The platform emphasizes secure, compliant handling of protected health information (SOC 2 Type 2, encryption in transit and at rest, role-based access, MFA) and single sign-on via Okta and Microsoft. Swift Medical does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal; integration is handled through direct engagement and enterprise SSO/EHR arrangements. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Tomorrow Health
providers.description: Tomorrow Health is an AI-powered platform for home-based care that connects providers, payors, and durable medical equipment (DMEPOS) suppliers, using intelligent automation to simplify ordering, routing, and reviewing home healthcare services. Its Horizon Suite includes AI Ordering, AI Fax Intake, and THEA (Tomorrow Health Expert Assistant). Headquartered in New York and backed by a16z, Bond Capital, and Obvious Ventures. No public developer API, SDK, or API documentation is currently published; the customer application is a private authenticated web app.

providers.name: 4baseCare
providers.description: 4baseCare is a precision oncology company founded in 2018, headquartered in Bengaluru, India with operations in Singapore, that combines next-generation-sequencing comprehensive genomic profiling with AI-driven clinical decision support to personalize cancer treatment. Its portfolio spans the TARGT family of tissue, liquid-biopsy and dual-source (SoLiQ) panels, germline and HRD testing, the OncoTwin AI insights layer, a Global Cancer Diversity Atlas of 30,000+ genomic profiles, molecular tumor board support, and the Oncobuddy patient program. Clinical results and decision support are delivered to oncologists through the Galens web portal at galens.4basecare.com. The company is Illumina Accelerator backed and closed a Series B round in 2024. As of the 2026-09-05 probe it publishes no developer program, no API documentation and no machine-readable API contract; the only API-shaped host, api.4basecare.com, is the private CodeIgniter application backend behind the Galens single-page app.

providers.name: Evidation Health
providers.description: Evidation Health is a San Mateo, California digital health company, founded in 2012, that measures health in everyday life and runs permissioned real-world data research at scale. Its consumer app and platform — Achievement — rewards members for connecting wearables, apps and health records, and its enterprise Research & Engagement Platform gives life-sciences, payer, government and non-profit customers eConsent and onboarding, ePRO and survey capture, passive and active device monitoring, program analytics, and participant education. Evidation combines data from sources including Apple Health, Fitbit, Garmin, Dexcom and EHR/claims records (via a partnership with 1upHealth's FHIR-based Patient Connect, and with HealthVerity), and has enabled 175+ virtual real-world studies and 70+ peer-reviewed publications. Evidation publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract; its programmatic surfaces are the member app backend and enterprise data deliveries, neither of which is publicly documented.

providers.name: HomeTouch
providers.description: HomeTouch (myhometouch.com) is a UK-based live-in home care marketplace founded in 2015 by Dr Jamie Wilson, a former NHS dementia specialist. The CQC-regulated service connects families with vetted professional carers for live-in, overnight, and visiting care, with a specialism in dementia and complex-needs support, hospital discharge, end-of-life, respite, and companionship care. Backed by 500 Global and other impact investors, HomeTouch operates a carer marketplace alongside a fully managed care service. The company publishes no public developer program or API; this profile tracks its identity, published web properties, and domain security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Leal Health (fka TrialJectory)
providers.description: Leal Health (formerly TrialJectory) is an AI-powered, patient-first decision-support platform that matches cancer patients to advanced treatments and clinical trials. Its patented natural language processing engine reads inclusion/exclusion eligibility criteria and connects to ClinicalTrials.gov so patients, caregivers, and oncologists can self-screen against every recruiting oncology trial in roughly two minutes. For pharma, biotech, and CRO customers, the Patient Match Optimizer SaaS dashboard delivers de-identified, aggregate real-time datasets on patient barriers, motivators, geography, and competitive landscape to shorten enrollment timelines and improve minority representation in trials. The company was founded as TrialJectory by Tzvia Bader (CEO), Avital Gaziel, Guy Gildor, and Noam Geva, later rebranded to Leal Health, and lists a Clifton, New Jersey mailing address. Leal Health operates no public developer program: a live platform API host exists at api.leal.health, but every path behind the root returns HTTP 401 and no OpenAPI, SDK, or developer documentation is published.

providers.name: 10x Genomics
providers.description: 10x Genomics is a life sciences technology company building instruments, reagents, and software that resolve biology at single-cell and spatial resolution. Its Chromium platform delivers single-cell gene expression, immune profiling, and multiomic analysis; its Visium and Xenium platforms deliver spatial transcriptomics and in situ single-cell spatial biology. The company supports researchers with analysis software (Cell Ranger, Space Ranger, Xenium Onboard Analysis, Loupe Browser), a cloud analysis platform, and open datasets. 10x Genomics does not publish a general-purpose public REST developer API; its developer surface is command-line analysis pipelines, file-format tooling, and open-source repositories on GitHub.

providers.name: Apero
providers.description: Apero Health is a San Francisco-based, Y Combinator-backed healthcare technology company that provides an integrated practice-management and revenue-cycle-management (RCM) platform for medical practices. Its cloud software unifies scheduling, clinical visit notes, insurance eligibility verification and claims billing, patient billing and payments, e-prescriptions, and financial reporting, and claims to reduce billing time by up to 80% while helping practices scale operations. Apero exposes a fully-featured REST API, webhooks, and CSV import that connect healthcare and finance workflows, and integrates with payers (Aetna, Cigna, UnitedHealthcare, Blue Cross Blue Shield) and platforms including Stripe, QuickBooks Online, Google, and Snowflake.

providers.name: Bristol Myers Squibb
providers.description: Bristol Myers Squibb (BMS) is a global Fortune 500 biopharmaceutical company committed to discovering, developing, and delivering innovative medicines for patients with serious diseases. BMS focuses on oncology, immunology, cardiovascular, fibrosis, and cell therapy (CAR T). The company operates BMS Study Connect for clinical trial recruitment, a Medical Information portal for healthcare providers, and the BMS Business Development platform for research partnerships and data sharing. BMS actively pursues technology partnerships in protein degradation, advanced treatment modalities, and digital health.

providers.name: Dandy
providers.description: Dandy is a digital dental lab platform for dentists, dental practices, and dental service organizations (DSOs). It combines intraoral scanner hardware, cloud-based case management software, and in-house dental lab manufacturing into a single scan-to-lab workflow. Dentists capture digital impressions with a Dandy intraoral scanner, submit cases through Dandy software, collaborate in real time with lab technicians via chat, video, and chairside scan review, and receive finished restorations manufactured by Dandy. Product lines include crowns, bridges, implants, clear aligners, retainers, dentures, night guards, splints, and sleep apnea devices. Dandy positions itself as an AI-powered digital dental lab modernizing restorative and orthodontic dentistry. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of General Catalyst and added to the API Evangelist network; the company publishes an agent-facing llms.txt and ai-index.json but does not currently expose a public developer API.

providers.name: ianacare
providers.description: ianacare ("iana" = I Am Not Alone) is a Boston-based caregiver support and navigation platform that sells to employers, health plans and providers as a benefit for the working family caregivers in their populations. Founded in 2018 by Jessica Kim and Steven Lee, it pairs a consumer mobile app — where a caregiver mobilizes an informal care team, coordinates practical tasks, unlocks employer benefits and finds local resources — with human Caregiver Navigators, and positions itself as a partner for fulfilling CMS GUIDE Model dementia-care requirements. The company raised a $12.1M Series A in January 2022 led by Greycroft with 8VC, SemperVirens, Able Partners and the Brown Angel Group. ianacare ships software only as an end-user product: the iOS and Android apps and the app.ianacare.com web client are backed by first-party hosts (iana.ianacare.com behind a JWT bearer token, api.ianacare.com behind a CloudFront 403) and by ianacare's own Auth0 custom domain auth.ianacare.com, which is the single machine-readable contract the company publishes. There is no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI, SDK, CLI, webhook catalog, MCP server or agent card on any ianacare host.

providers.name: Opalite Health
providers.description: Opalite Health is building the language layer for healthcare. Its platform delivers real-time, AI-powered medical interpretation across 150+ languages, validated against certified human interpreters and engineered for HIPAA-aligned, clinical-grade use. Opalite connects providers and patients with limited English proficiency in seconds — through EHR workflows and rapid healthcare deployment — to close language gaps that drive health inequities and poor outcomes. The company publishes a marketing and validation-study presence but does not operate a public developer API program; api.opalitehealth.com is a private application backend. This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and enriched with the company's real identity, compliance posture (HIPAA, SOC 2 Type II, AES-256 encryption), and domain-security probes.

providers.name: Qualifyze
providers.description: Qualifyze is a supplier risk management and audit platform for the life sciences and pharmaceutical industries. It helps quality, procurement, and compliance teams qualify suppliers faster, run and manage GxP audits globally, and monitor supplier risk continuously. Its Audit Management Platform streamlines audit execution, CAPA management, and real-time visibility with access to a shared library of 5,000+ audit reports, while its Quality Insights Platform layers AI-driven predictive risk monitoring on top of the supply chain. Qualifyze is a delivered SaaS product for enterprise life-sciences customers; it exposes no public developer API, portal, or documentation at this time. The company publishes ISO 9001, ISO 27001, and SOC 2 compliance posture.

providers.name: Uno Health
providers.description: Uno Health is a New York-based healthcare technology company that helps Medicare members enroll in the government assistance programs they are eligible for — such as SNAP and utility assistance — saving members an average of $4,500 per year. Medicare Advantage health plans partner with Uno's technology-driven member engagement platform to simplify eligibility checks, subsidy enrollment, plan optimization, and benefits matching, increasing Part C revenue, member retention, and star ratings. Members run a 5-minute savings check, upload enrollment documents, and track recurring monthly savings through the Uno Health Member Portal. Backed by Cowboy Ventures and General Catalyst. Uno Health publishes no public developer program; its API (api.unohealth.com, AWS API Gateway) is private and partner-facing.

providers.name: Alpha Sophia
providers.description: Alpha Sophia provides a comprehensive healthcare commercial intelligence platform, offering detailed data on providers, organizations, and market insights across pharma, biotech, medtech, and related sectors. Their API enables searchable access to extensive provider profiles, procedure volumes, licensing information, and more, supporting sales, marketing, research, and investment decision-making.

providers.name: Cleerly
providers.description: Cleerly is a digital healthcare company building an AI-powered platform for the diagnosis and management of coronary artery disease (heart disease). Its software analyzes coronary CT angiography (CCTA) imaging to automatically quantify and characterize atherosclerotic plaque, measure stenosis severity, and stage disease, giving physicians a precise, personalized picture of a patient's heart-disease risk. The goal is to move heart-disease care from symptom-based testing toward direct measurement of plaque, reducing unnecessary invasive procedures while improving diagnostic accuracy. Cleerly operates as an enterprise clinical SaaS delivered to health systems, cardiologists, and imaging centers rather than a public developer API program; it publishes a marketing and clinical-evidence site plus a clinician-facing application (Cleerly Labs) and a public trust center. Cleerly is backed by Battery Ventures and Insight Partners.

providers.name: Floy
providers.description: Floy is a Munich-based healthcare AI company (founded 2021) that builds AI-powered radiology software for medical imaging. Its two products — opportunistic screening and diagnostic assistance — analyse CT and MRI examinations to surface additional findings beyond the initial radiologist assessment, enabling earlier diagnosis and better patient outcomes. The models are trained on 17 million medical examinations. Floy is an ISO 13485:2016 certified, EU MDR Class IIb medical-device manufacturer and is GDPR compliant, with research partnerships including DKFZ, LMU Klinikum Munich, Stanford, and the University of Oxford. It is backed by HV Capital, 10x Founders, xdeck, and Acurio Ventures. Floy is a clinical B2B product and does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Peppy
providers.description: Peppy is a global employee healthcare benefits platform, delivered through a mobile app, that connects workers with specialist clinicians across key life stages. Offered by employers as a benefit, Peppy provides unlimited access to practitioners covering women's health, men's health, fertility, pregnancy and early parenthood, menopause, and neurodiversity, alongside lifestyle support for nutrition, fitness, and mental wellbeing. Peppy operates a consumer and employer facing service and does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its published web properties and security posture. Peppy is a Seedcamp portfolio company.

providers.name: Stepful
providers.description: Stepful is a New York-based healthcare workforce education company that trains people with a high-school education for entry-level allied-health roles in as little as four months. It runs live, cohort-based online programs — Medical Assistant, Pharmacy Technician, Patient Care Technician, Medical Administrative Assistant, Surgical Technologist, Dental Assistant, Phlebotomy Technician, Sterile Processing and Practical Nursing — pairing virtual instructor-led classes and 1:1 coaching with at-home clinical skills kits, employer-site clinical rotations and an AI-assisted practice platform, then places graduates into hospital and clinic jobs. Its "School-as-a-Service" employer product lets health systems stand up in-house training and upskilling pipelines. Stepful is backed by Y Combinator, Oak HC/FT and Reach Capital, has raised a $31.5M Series B and a $55M Series C, and reports having served more than 30,000 students. It is a Delaware corporation approved to operate by state career-school boards in Alabama, California, Indiana, Kentucky, Michigan, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Texas and Utah. Stepful publishes no public developer API: its student classroom and staff admin applications are both authenticated-only, and no OpenAPI, GraphQL, MCP or webhook contract is served from any host it controls.

providers.name: Stryker
providers.description: Stryker Corporation is a Fortune 500 medical technologies company offering products in orthopedics, medical and surgical equipment, and neurotechnology and spine. Stryker provides Connected OR integration platforms and Smart Equipment Management (SEM) systems for healthcare facilities. The company does not currently offer a publicly documented developer API. Stryker's digital health products include the Mako robotic arm for orthopedic surgery, iSuite integrated OR technology, and asset tracking systems. Integration with hospital EHR and OR management systems is done through vendor partnerships rather than public APIs.

providers.name: GT Medical Technologies
providers.description: GT Medical Technologies, Inc. is a Tempe, Arizona medical device company founded by brain tumor specialists to commercialize GammaTile, an FDA-cleared, bioabsorbable collagen implant embedded with Cesium-131 radiation seeds. Surgeons place the tiles directly into the resection cavity at the time of brain tumor removal, delivering immediate, targeted radiation without the weeks-long healing delay conventional external beam radiotherapy requires. The company sells a physical, prescription-only implant to hospitals and neurosurgical centers through a direct sales force and a Salesforce-based ordering portal; it publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Ultromics
providers.description: Ultromics is a UK-based clinical AI company, spun out of the University of Oxford and backed by GV, whose EchoGo platform applies FDA 510(k)-cleared AI to routine echocardiograms to help clinicians detect heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and cardiac amyloidosis. EchoGo integrates into existing hospital echo workflows and PACS environments, delivering results through clinical systems rather than a public developer API.

providers.name: Virta Health
providers.description: Virta Health is a virtual, nutrition-first healthcare company delivering sustainable weight loss and type 2 diabetes reversal. Its program combines personalized nutrition plans, continuous expert health coaching, physician-led medication management, and connected devices, delivered through a consumer mobile app and sold to employers, health plans, and healthcare providers. Virta is HITRUST- and SOC 2 Type II-certified and operates as a HIPAA-covered clinical service. As of this enrichment pass Virta publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification surface; this profile captures its public identity, security posture, and compliance certifications.

providers.name: Allara
providers.description: Allara Health is a virtual women's healthcare platform focused on complex hormonal, metabolic, and gynecological conditions such as PCOS, insulin resistance, endometriosis, thyroid disorders, menopause, and PMDD. Serving more than 85,000 patients across 45 states and D.C., Allara connects members with board-certified OB-GYNs, endocrinologists, women's health nurse practitioners, and registered dietitians for virtual consultations, advanced hormonal and metabolic lab testing, personalized treatment plans, and ongoing care coordination. The company operates consumer-facing web and patient portal applications; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time. Added to the API Evangelist network as an index-ventures portfolio company.

providers.name: Aluna
providers.description: Aluna is a digital respiratory health company behind an FDA-cleared, portable Bluetooth spirometer and companion mobile app that let people with asthma, COPD, and cystic fibrosis measure lung function (FEV1) at home and share the results with their care teams. The platform pairs a hospital-grade sensor with a gamified app and machine-learning analytics to encourage proper technique, track symptoms, triggers, and medications, and surface trends that help clinicians intervene before an exacerbation. Founded by Charvi Shetty and Inderjit Jutla out of UC Berkeley's bioengineering program, Aluna raised a $15.3M Series B and is a Matrix Partners portfolio company; the product is now operated under Huma Therapeutics. Aluna publishes consumer, clinical-provider, and clinical-trial surfaces but no public developer API.

providers.name: Big Sky Health
providers.description: Big Sky Health (now operating as Zero Longevity Science, Inc.) is a Bozeman, Montana consumer digital-health company best known for Zero, one of the most popular intermittent-fasting and nutrition-tracking mobile apps. Zero combines a fasting timer, photo-based meal and protein logging, a personalized Protein Score, and water-intake tracking to help users manage body composition and adopt science-backed longevity practices. The company runs as a direct-to-consumer mobile subscription business (Zero Plus) on iOS and Android. As of this profile it publishes no public developer API, SDK, MCP server, or developer program. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a Trinity Ventures portfolio company awaiting enrichment.

providers.name: Birches Health
providers.description: Birches Health is a fully virtual behavioral addiction treatment provider specializing in gambling disorder and related compulsive behaviors such as sports betting, day trading, video gaming, and pornography. Founded in 2023 and headquartered in Phoenix, Arizona, the company delivers confidential online care from licensed gambling counselors, peer mentors, financial coaches, and group therapy across all 50 states. Birches Health partners with 18+ state governments that have legalized sports betting and 100+ national insurance plans (including UnitedHealthcare, Cigna, Aetna, and Blue Cross Blue Shield) so most clients pay $0-25 per session, with a core program completed in about 12 weeks. The company has raised approximately $20M from AlleyCorp, General Catalyst, and Will Ventures. Birches Health does not currently publish a public developer API, portal, or specification; this profile captures its identity and public web surface.

providers.name: Dragonfly Therapeutics
providers.description: Dragonfly Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company based in Waltham, Massachusetts, founded in 2016 by Tyler Jacks, Bill Haney and David Raulet to develop natural killer (NK) cell-based immunotherapies. Its proprietary TriNKET (Tri-specific NK cell Engager Therapy) and cytokine engager platforms produce molecules that bind both a tumor or disease antigen and an NK cell activating receptor, recruiting innate and adaptive immunity against cancer, autoimmune disease, fibrosis and neuro-inflammation. Lead clinical candidate DF1001 targets HER2 in advanced solid tumors, and the platform is licensed under multi-target collaborations with AbbVie, Bristol Myers Squibb, Merck and Gilead. Dragonfly is a therapeutics developer rather than a software company: it publishes no developer program, no public API, no SDKs and no machine-readable API contract. The only agent-readable surfaces on its own host are the llms.txt and Model Context Protocol endpoint automatically provisioned by its Wix website platform.

providers.name: Faro
providers.description: Faro Health is an AI platform for clinical development that helps biopharma and clinical research teams design and execute better studies. Founded in 2019 and headquartered in San Diego, California, Faro provides study design optimization, automated protocol document authoring, and clinical workflow automation, digitizing and structuring trial protocols so teams can accelerate development without compromising scientific rigor, patient safety, or patient-centricity. Faro is backed by investors including General Catalyst.

providers.name: Floreo
providers.description: Floreo is a research-based virtual reality (VR) digital therapeutics company that delivers immersive lessons teaching social, behavioral, communication, and life skills to neurodiverse individuals, including autistic children and adults. The platform runs across mobile (iPhone with Google Cardboard) and standalone VR headsets (Meta Quest 2/3/Pro, PICO), with a companion clinician portal for supervised sessions, progress tracking, and telehealth-style delivery. Floreo holds an FDA Breakthrough Device designation and participates in the FDA Total Product Life Cycle Advisory Program (TAP), and works with schools, behavioral-health providers, Medicaid programs, and research partners. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta; the company publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK at this time.

providers.name: Framewise Health
providers.description: Framewise Health is an AI-native patient engagement platform (Y Combinator, Spring 2026) that converts a patient's medical records into personalized, clinically-reviewed educational videos. The platform pulls patient data from electronic health records over any FHIR R4 endpoint, generates discharge and treatment-adherence education tailored to the individual using institutional protocols and drug-information databases, and delivers it by SMS in 75+ languages with no app and no login. It then tracks patient comprehension in real time, giving care teams engagement data to flag which patients need follow-up. Framewise integrates with Epic, Oracle Health (Cerner), Athenahealth, ModMed, eClinicalWorks, and NextGen, and is HIPAA and SOC 2 compliant with an AWS BAA and end-to-end encryption. It targets hospitals, pharmaceutical companies, medical device manufacturers, and private clinics seeking to improve patient outcomes and medication adherence.

providers.name: Headlight
providers.description: Headlight is a US mental health services company delivering teletherapy, in-person therapy, psychiatry, and medication management through a clinician-centered care model. Founded by Drs. Manish Sheth and Shashita Inamdar, it helps patients move from initial interest to a well-matched therapist or prescriber with less friction, treating conditions including depression, anxiety, ADHD, bipolar disorder, PTSD, trauma, OCD, panic disorder, postpartum depression, and insomnia. Headlight is in-network with major insurers (Aetna, Blue Cross, Cigna, UnitedHealthcare, Humana, Kaiser, Moda) and operates across Alaska, California, Colorado, Oregon, Texas, and Washington. The company raised $18M led by Matrix and EPIC Ventures. This is a consumer clinical services provider with no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Homage
providers.description: Homage is a Singapore-headquartered holistic health and caregiving platform that connects families with screened, professional caregivers, nurses, and therapists to deliver personal care, home nursing procedures, rehabilitation, and health services where people live. Founded in 2016, Homage operates across Singapore, Malaysia, and Australia through consumer mobile apps and a care-management operations platform, offering flexible on-demand and recurring visits, care assessments, custom care plans, and teleconsultations for conditions such as dementia, stroke recovery, and post-surgical care. Homage does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI definition; this profile captures its public web properties and probed domain security.

providers.name: Kismet
providers.description: Kismet is an Australian digital-health marketplace that connects people with disability — primarily National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS) participants — to verified, available service providers across occupational therapy, speech therapy, physiotherapy, support coordination and plan management. The platform pairs a searchable provider marketplace and care index with a Concierge AI matching service that builds a shortlist of suitable, available providers within 48 hours, alongside budget-tracking and plan-management tools for participants. Kismet is backed by Prosus Ventures and ships consumer iOS and Android apps. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub; no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: MedHOK (Hearst Communications)
providers.description: MHK (formerly MedHOK), part of Hearst Health, is a healthcare technology company providing a unified SaaS platform for health plans and payers. Its CareProminence suite spans utilization management, care management, complaints/appeals and grievances, pharmacy management, population health and quality management, and interoperability (the MHK Interop Suite), while its MarketProminence suite covers enrollment and member maintenance, premium billing, financial reconciliation, and member web portals. MHK helps Medicare, Medicaid, and commercial health plans streamline operations, ensure regulatory compliance, and improve the member experience. The MHK Interop Suite supports FHIR, SMART on FHIR, Da Vinci, and CMS-0057 interoperability requirements. MHK publishes HITRUST and ISO 27001 certification and NCQA prevalidation. The company operates a public marketing and resource site but does not publish a public developer portal or API program.

providers.name: nference
providers.description: nference is a healthcare-AI company that builds an agentic intelligence layer for clinical research and drug development. Its nSights platform aggregates and analyzes de-identified multimodal patient data at massive scale — 1.4 billion+ clinical notes, 10 billion+ radiology images, 20 million+ digitized pathology whole-slide images, 12 million+ ECG waveforms, and 100 million+ echocardiogram videos — extracting 30,000+ clinical biomarkers to help life-sciences and health-system partners design patient cohorts, explore patient journeys, annotate data for model development, and run advanced data-science workflows across cardiology, oncology, immunology, rare diseases, neurology, infectious diseases, and nephrology. nference spun out the venture companies Anumana (ECG-based biomarker discovery) and Pramana (digital pathology). The company operates as an enterprise B2B platform with no public self-serve API; it is profiled here for its security, compliance, and governance posture. Backed by Matrix Partners.

providers.name: Prenuvo
providers.description: Prenuvo operates a preventive healthcare screening service built around whole-body MRI imaging paired with blood biomarker panels and personalized results reviews. A single scan captures on the order of a billion data points while screening for hundreds of conditions across major organ systems, without radiation or contrast agents, and completes in under an hour. Blood panels measure 80+ biomarkers tied to inflammation, hormone levels, and metabolic health, with optional advanced imaging for brain, heart, and body composition. Prenuvo runs clinics across the US, Canada, Australia, and the UK, and works with research institutions including Mount Sinai, UCLA, Johns Hopkins, Stanford, and Penn. Prenuvo does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Summer Health
providers.description: Summer Health is a pediatric health company offering families fast, board-certified pediatric care. Its flagship consumer service provides comprehensive at-home blood work for children ages 8-18 (one blood draw covering 74 biomarkers) reviewed by board-certified pediatricians over video, alongside text-based urgent-care messaging with pediatric clinicians. The service is HSA/FSA eligible and LegitScript-approved. Summer Health is a consumer-facing telehealth offering and does not currently publish a public developer program, API documentation, or third-party integration surface. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lux Capital and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Teal Health
providers.description: Teal Health, Inc. is a women's health company behind the Teal Wand, the first and only FDA-approved at-home self-collection device for cervical cancer screening in the United States. Its end-to-end telehealth service pairs the self-collection kit with virtual Teal medical providers who prescribe the kit, review Roche cobas HPV lab results, and support patients aged 25-65 throughout the screening experience. Now available in all 50 states, Teal Health runs a HIPAA-compliant direct-to-consumer telehealth platform and is a consumer of third-party healthcare APIs (Healthie for scheduling/telehealth, Candid for billing) rather than a publisher of a public developer API.

providers.name: Cadence Solutions
providers.description: Cadence Solutions, Inc. — operating as Cadence — is a New York-based clinical AI and remote patient monitoring company founded in 2020 by Chris Altchek. Cadence partners with large health systems and payers to deliver continuous chronic-care management between clinic visits: FDA-cleared connected devices (blood pressure cuffs, glucometers, weight scales) stream daily vitals to a 24/7 clinical care team backed by supervised AI agents that flag out-of-range readings, close care gaps, and escalate to clinicians for medication titration. The platform covers hypertension, type 2 diabetes, heart failure and COPD, is integrated two-way into partner EHRs (Epic, Oracle Cerner, athenahealth), and supports Medicare RPM/CCM and the CMS ACCESS model. Cadence serves more than 100,000 patients across systems including Community Health Systems, LifePoint Health, Providence, Rush, MemorialCare, Corewell Health, Ardent Health and Duke Health. It raised a $100M Series C led by Spark Capital in June 2026 ($241M total, ~$1.23B valuation). Cadence publishes no public developer program or API: EHR interoperability is delivered as bilateral health system integrations, not a self-serve API surface.

providers.name: Curevo
providers.description: Curevo is a clinical‑stage biotechnology company that operates a global healthcare marketplace, connecting patients with verified medical centers, doctors, and wellness providers across more than 150 countries. The platform offers a range of treatments—from cardiology and oncology to regenerative therapies such as stem cell, hyperbaric oxygen, and blood ozonation—facilitating transparent pricing, tele‑assist AI support, and end‑to‑end medical travel coordination.

providers.name: Health Resources and Services Administration
providers.description: The Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA) is the primary Federal agency for improving access to health care services for people who are uninsured, isolated, or medically vulnerable. HRSA provides data and web services for healthcare resources, facility locations, and program information.

providers.name: Lantern
providers.description: Lantern (legal entity Employer Direct Healthcare, LLC dba Lantern Specialty Care) is a US specialty care platform that connects members with high-quality, lower-cost care for surgery, cancer and infusion therapy — the complex, high-cost episodes that account for roughly half of healthcare spending. Founded in 2011 as SurgeryPlus and later expanded into cancer and infusion care, Lantern sells to employers, public-sector employers, labor union trusts, health plans and benefits consultants, pairing a hand-selected "Network of Excellence" of specialists with dedicated care teams that navigate a member end to end through a treatment journey. Lantern is backed by Insight Partners. As of this enrichment pass Lantern publishes no public developer program, API documentation, machine-readable specification, SDKs or discovery surface — this profile captures its public company, trust and security posture only.

providers.name: Md Ally
providers.description: MD Ally is a New York-based digital health company that integrates telehealth into the 911 emergency response system. Its platform lets emergency dispatchers route low-acuity, non-emergency callers to a virtual care tier, connecting patients with telehealth clinicians, in-network resources, and social services instead of dispatching EMS or defaulting to an emergency-room visit. MD Ally works with public safety agencies and payers to expand traditional two-tier dispatch models, reduce unnecessary ambulance transports and ER visits, and improve patient navigation. Backed by General Catalyst and Techstars.

providers.name: Parambil
providers.description: Parambil provides AI-powered medical record review software that accelerates and improves accuracy in mass tort and complex litigation workflows. The platform generates comprehensive chronologies, case validations, and analytic insights, reviewing over 5 million records with 44% higher data correctness and 95% faster processing than traditional methods. Trusted by plaintiff and defense firms, Parambil’s solution helps legal teams streamline evidence analysis and reduce costs.

providers.name: Transcarent
providers.description: Transcarent is a health and care experience company serving self-insured employers, health plans, and government and labor union clients. Its consumer-facing platform, WayFinding, combines generative AI agents with instant access to human health guides and clinicians to deliver benefits navigation, clinical guidance, virtual primary and specialty care, pharmacy care, surgery care, cancer care, weight-health programs, and 2nd.MD second opinions in a single experience. The platform is built on an API-first, cloud-native architecture with pre-built HL7 FHIR and EDI connectors that integrate with existing eligibility files and medical, pharmacy, and point-solution benefits. Transcarent exposes these integrations to enterprise partners rather than through a public self-serve developer API or documentation portal.

providers.name: Axsome Therapeutics
providers.description: Axsome Therapeutics (NASDAQ: AXSM) is a biopharmaceutical company developing and delivering novel therapies for the management of central nervous system (CNS) disorders. Headquartered at One World Trade Center, New York, Axsome markets three FDA-approved products — Auvelity (dextromethorphan-bupropion) for major depressive disorder, Sunosi (solriamfetol) for excessive daytime sleepiness in narcolepsy and obstructive sleep apnea, and Symbravo (meloxicam-rizatriptan) for the acute treatment of migraine — and is advancing a pipeline including AXS-05 for Alzheimer's disease agitation and smoking cessation, AXS-12 (reboxetine) for narcolepsy, and AXS-14 (esreboxetine) for fibromyalgia. Axsome operates a corporate website and product / HCP microsites but does not expose a public developer API surface; this profile catalogs corporate, product, regulatory, and investor touchpoints rather than programmatic interfaces.

providers.name: Careharmony
providers.description: CareHarmony is a chronic care management company delivering coordinated, personalized health services. Their mission is to make personalized, coordinated care possible for every patient through fee‑for‑service programs, remote patient monitoring, and value‑based care solutions. They offer chronic care management, preventive care programs, annual wellness visits, transitional care management, and address social determinants of health.

providers.name: Clivi
providers.description: Clivi is Mexico's largest digital clinic for diabetes and obesity care, delivering fully online telehealth treatment that combines endocrinologists, internists, nutritionists, and psychologists with continuous glucose monitoring and GLP-1 medications (Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro, Saxenda, Rybelsus). Founded in 2020 and based in Mexico City, Clivi serves patients nationwide through WhatsApp-based virtual care, home medication delivery via its Farmacia Clivi digital pharmacy, and tiered treatment plans (Clivi Pro, Plus, Total, and Zero). Backed by 500 Global and other investors, Clivi operates as a consumer healthtech service; it publishes no public developer API, but does expose an llms.txt content index for AI agents.

providers.name: DynamiCare Health
providers.description: DynamiCare Health provides technology solutions for substance use recovery, offering digital therapeutics, contingency management, and support tools for individuals, families, and health plans. Their platform integrates evidence‑based interventions, insurance navigation, and outcome tracking to improve recovery outcomes.

providers.name: kelaHealth
providers.description: kelaHealth is a healthcare AI company that improves surgical outcomes through its Surgical Intelligence Service, an AI-enabled API delivering patient-specific predictive insights at critical decision points across the perioperative process. Models trained on millions of surgical procedures predict individual patient risk across nine major complication categories, identify modifiable factors, and recommend stratified interventions tailored to hospital standards. The service integrates into existing medtech and healthcare software applications using EHR, robotic, and social-determinants-of-health data to help providers improve growth, efficiency, quality, and safety. kelaHealth is HIPAA compliant and backed by Techstars. It does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or SDKs; its API is delivered through partner integrations.

providers.name: Nomi Health
providers.description: Nomi Health is a Utah-based direct healthcare and healthcare fintech company founded in 2019 that operates a payments, claims and analytics platform for self-funded employers, health plans, brokers and providers. Its stack spans real-time provider payments and claims adjudication (Healthcare Financial Services), directly contracted provider networks (Direct Network / Open Network), benefits-data analytics through Artemis by Nomi Health, and direct patient care services. Nomi Health operates authenticated web portals for providers, members and employers, but publishes no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Prax Health
providers.description: Prax Health is a healthcare platform that helps nurse practitioners launch and grow their own independent practices. It provides an all-in-one back office that handles business formation, regulatory and clinical compliance, medical billing, insurance credentialing, an integrated EHR, and ongoing practice consulting. The company's stated mission is to put healthcare back in the hands of providers by removing the administrative and operational burden that keeps clinicians from practicing independently. Prax Health is a venture-backed company (Canaan Partners) and operates a consumer/clinician web application rather than a public developer platform; as of this profile it exposes no public API, SDKs, or developer documentation.

providers.name: Unobravo
providers.description: Unobravo is Europe's largest online psychology service, founded in 2019 by psychologist Danila De Stefano. It matches people with one of 9,500+ individually vetted psychologists and psychotherapists for individual, couples, and group therapy delivered online, serving Italy, Spain, and France as well as Italians abroad, with 500,000+ people supported across more than 10 million online sessions, plus a B2B mental-wellbeing offering (Unobravo Business) and an ECM training academy. Backed by Insight Partners and Northzone. Its backend API (api.unobravo.com) is private, with no public developer surface.

providers.name: Voom Medical Devices
providers.description: Voom Medical Devices, Inc. is an orthopedic medical device and surgical innovation company founded by bunion surgeon Dr. Neal Blitz and headquartered in Brentwood, Tennessee. Voom designs implants and procedural systems for minimally invasive bunion surgery (MIBS) and foot-and-ankle reconstruction, including the patented Revcon non-compression dual-zone bone screw system, the Bunionplasty 360 Bunion Repair procedure, and the MIBS CoPilot Shift + Targeting Guide single-use sterile kit. The company sells to surgeons and hospitals, runs a surgeon training program, and operates the patient-facing Bunionplasty.com procedure site with a doctor locator. It is a physical device manufacturer: it publishes no developer portal, no API documentation and no machine-readable API contract on any host it controls.

providers.name: AgentifAI
providers.description: AgentifAI is a Portuguese enterprise conversational-AI company, headquartered in Braga, that builds AliceOS - a voice-first AI contact-center and autonomous agent platform purpose-built for the regulated banking and healthcare sectors. AliceOS is sold as a managed enterprise deployment rather than a self-serve developer product: it orchestrates multi-agent workflows across phone, WhatsApp, SMS, email and web, and integrates with core banking systems, CRMs, fraud engines, Hospital Information Systems and EMR/EHR platforms over REST, SOAP and OAuth, with SIP and CTI telephony adapters. Reference deployments include Santander, Banco BPI, Caixa Geral de Depositos, Vivalto Sante, Lusiadas Saude and Luz Saude. The company publishes a first-party llms.txt and a SafeBase trust center naming SOC 2 Type 2, ISO/IEC 27001, ISO/IEC 42001:2023, PCI DSS v4.0.0 and HIPAA, but no public developer portal, API reference or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Blackrock Neurotech
providers.description: Blackrock Neurotech is a Salt Lake City, Utah based neurotechnology company that designs and manufactures implantable brain-computer interface (BCI) systems and the research instrumentation around them. Its platform pairs Utah Array microelectrode arrays and the next-generation Neuralace interface with the NeuroPort, Cerebus and CerePlex Direct neural signal processors, the CereStim stimulation system, and the Central software suite for acquisition, visualization and offline spike sorting. The company reports more than 19 years of human clinical study, 1,000+ research institutions served and 2,000+ published studies using its hardware. Blackrock does not publish a public web API: its programmatic surface is a set of device and file-format libraries distributed as downloads and GitHub source (cbSDK C++ API, cbMEX MATLAB API, CereStim API, brPY/brpylib Python data loader, and the NPMK MATLAB toolkit). Enrichment probing on 2026-08-02 found no OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL, MCP, agent card, llms.txt or /.well-known/ discovery surface on any Blackrock host.

providers.name: Cleardata
providers.description: ClearDATA is healthcare's dedicated cloud security, compliance, and operations partner, helping providers, payers, health-tech software companies, medical device makers, and life sciences organizations build and run on AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud in a HIPAA- and HITRUST-aligned way. Its offering spans Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM) with 300+ healthcare-specific safeguards, Managed Detection & Response (MDR), automated Cloud Compliance, and Cloud Operations, delivered through the CyberHealth platform and managed/professional services. ClearDATA is an AWS Level 1 MSSP and Microsoft Gold Partner, and maps controls to HIPAA, HITRUST, SOC 2, NIST, ISO, PCI, and GDPR. ClearDATA is backed by Norwest Venture Partners. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; ClearDATA does not publish a public developer API or portal.

providers.name: DayDream Dental
providers.description: DayDream Dental is a full-service dental billing and revenue cycle management (RCM) provider that runs the insurance and billing operations for dental practices and DSOs so clinical teams can focus on patient care. Services span insurance verification with custom coding breakdowns saved directly to the practice management system (PMS), clean claims submission with attachments and narratives, payment posting with accurate insurance adjustments, diligent claim follow-up every seven days until paid with denials appealed, and patient billing via text, email, and mail. DayDream operates a HIPAA-focused trust center and a client dashboard app, and publishes a blog, CDT-code and payer references, videos, and demo scheduling for onboarding new offices. This is a service company rather than an API provider — it publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI.

providers.name: Oviva
providers.description: Oviva is a European digital health company, founded in 2014, delivering personalized, dietitian-led care for people managing type 2 diabetes, obesity, and other diet-related conditions. It combines a mobile app for logging food, activity, and progress with human coaching from a network of 420+ dietitians, psychologists, and doctors, operating across the UK, Germany, and Switzerland and serving 900K+ people. Oviva is delivered as a regulated digital therapeutic (CE-marked, ISO 27001, NHS DTAC and CQC assessed) rather than through a public developer API; this profile captures its security, compliance, and legal surface. Backed by Partech.

providers.name: Rx Redefined
providers.description: Rx Redefined Inc is a healthcare technology company in Arroyo Grande, California, founded in 2018, that operates a patented, compliance-focused DMEPOS (durable medical equipment, prosthetics, orthotics and supplies) platform for physicians. The platform lets a medical practice become a licensed physician-owned DMEPOS supplier and distribute medical supplies — insulin pumps, breast pumps, ostomy pouches, urinary catheters — directly to its own patients instead of handing the order to a third-party supplier. It ships two products: a Full-Service product built around physician personal performance, and an In-Office product built around the in-office ancillary services exception. The platform covers CMS licensing onboarding, electronic ordering with per-order compliance and eligibility checks, supply-chain integration with 10+ U.S. distribution centers, and end-to-end revenue-cycle and audit management. The company reports use across 350+ U.S. clinics and runs on ISO 27001 certified infrastructure with HIPAA controls. The product is a customer-only web application at app.rxredefined.com; Rx Redefined publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: Viome
providers.description: Viome (Viome Life Sciences) is a health technology company founded in 2016 by Naveen Jain that uses metatranscriptomic RNA sequencing — a technique originally developed for biodefense at Los Alamos National Laboratory — combined with artificial intelligence to measure active gene expression across the gut microbiome, oral microbiome, and human cells. From at-home stool, saliva, and finger-prick blood samples the company produces over 50 health scores across eight categories (BioAge, Gut Health, Oral Health, Energy, Inflammaging, Mood/Memory/Focus, Immunity, and Heart and Metabolic Health), personalized food recommendations across more than 370 foods, and custom-blended precision supplements and biotics. Products include the Full Body Intelligence, Gut Intelligence, and Oral Health Intelligence tests plus the CancerDetect saliva screening test for oral and throat cancer. Viome operates in over 100 countries, publishes peer-reviewed research in NPJ Genomic Medicine, iScience, and Microbiome, and runs a Life Sciences research division. Viome publishes no public developer API or machine-readable API contract; its consumer app at my.viome.com is served by an undocumented private backend, and the only agent-facing artifact the company publishes is a curated llms.txt.

providers.name: Denticon
providers.description: Denticon is a cloud-based dental practice management platform built for dental service organizations (DSOs) and multi-location group practices, owned and operated by Planet DDS (which also owns Cloud 9 Ortho and Apteryx imaging). The Denticon API program - relaunched in July 2024 on a new developer portal powered by Azure API Management - exposes RESTful APIs, webhooks, and batch data extracts covering patient, appointment, financial/ledger, insurance and claims (Revenue Cycle Management), clinical, and practice/office data, with OAuth 2.0 auth, an event-driven architecture for synchronized updates, and writebacks into Denticon. API access is partner-gated - Planet DDS must approve vendors and each client practice authorizes vendor access to specific office locations (OIDs). Public documentation exists, but keys and interactive access require program enrollment, so the endpoint surface below is modeled from the published API categories rather than a downloadable OpenAPI specification.

providers.name: Field Medical
providers.description: Field Medical, Inc. is a Carlsbad, California clinical-stage cardiac electrophysiology company founded in 2022 by Dr. Steven Mickelsen to build a second-generation pulsed field ablation (PFA) platform. Its FieldForce Ablation System pairs a focal catheter design with proprietary FieldBending energy and is positioned as the first PFA system purpose-built for ventricular arrhythmia ablation, with atrial fibrillation applications in development. The company holds FDA Breakthrough Device Designation and a place in the FDA TAP Pilot Program for its VT indication, has published first-in-human VCAS data in Circulation, and has raised roughly $75M across Series A and Series B. Field Medical is a medical device manufacturer, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer portal, no public REST/GraphQL API and no SDKs. Its only machine-readable public surface is the llms.txt and anonymous site MCP endpoint that its Wix-hosted corporate website serves.

providers.name: OpenEvidence
providers.description: OpenEvidence is a clinical decision-support search platform that uses generative AI grounded in peer-reviewed medical literature to answer clinical questions for verified clinicians. The product is free for U.S. licensed clinicians and is monetized through pharmaceutical advertising; partnerships include the New England Journal of Medicine, JAMA, NCCN, and the Cochrane Library. As of 2026 it serves more than 860,000 verified clinicians. OpenEvidence does not currently expose a public self-service developer API.

providers.name: Stericycle
providers.description: Stericycle is a Fortune 500 compliance company specializing in regulated medical waste disposal, sharps management, pharmaceutical waste, secure information destruction, and healthcare compliance training. In November 2024, Stericycle was acquired by Waste Management (WM) for approximately $7.2 billion. The company operates as WM Healthcare Solutions division, serving hospitals, clinics, medical offices, dental practices, veterinary facilities, and other healthcare organizations. Stericycle's MyStericycle customer portal enables online account management, scheduling, compliance training, and billing.

providers.name: symplr
providers.description: symplr (symplr software LLC, Houston) sells healthcare operations software to hospitals, health systems and payers: provider data management and credentialing (symplr Provider, Directory, CVO, Payer), workforce and talent management (Smart Square, symplr Workforce, formerly API Healthcare), quality and safety (Midas), clinical communications, spend, access, contract and compliance management, unified as the symplr Operations Platform. It markets APIs, webhooks and a certified partner program, but publishes no public API reference or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Telesair
providers.description: Telesair, Inc. is a Southern California MedTech company, founded in 2020 and headquartered in Irvine, California, that builds respiratory care hardware for patients with respiratory insufficiency. Its flagship product is Bonhawa, a purpose-built High Flow Oxygen Therapy (HFOT) respiratory humidifier that delivers warmed and humidified respiratory gases to spontaneously breathing pediatric and adult patients (10 kg and up) across a 2-80 L/min flow range, with separate pediatric and adult modes, a streamlined disinfection process and a touchscreen interface. Bonhawa holds both FDA 510(k) clearance (October 2023) and the CE Mark under the European Medical Device Regulation (August 2023), and is distributed to US hospitals under an exclusive agreement with Tri-anim Health Services. Telesair also supplies AVEA disposable expiratory filters. Telesair is a medical device manufacturer rather than a software vendor: it publishes no developer portal, no API reference and no machine-readable API contract. Its only machine-readable agent surface is the Wix platform's Site Visitor Assistant MCP endpoint and an llms.txt served from its own marketing host.

providers.name: 28 labs
providers.description: 28labs Inc. operates She's Well (sheswell.co), a consumer fertility-care platform that bundles egg freezing, fertility testing, IVF coordination, clinic visits, labs, medications, and concierge nurse support into a single transparent subscription plan starting at $249/month over up to 60 months. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. It is a business-to-consumer digital-health service with no public developer platform, API, SDKs, or developer documentation at this time; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Docquity
providers.description: Docquity is a Singapore-headquartered digital health company operating Asia's largest verified professional network for licensed healthcare practitioners, with more than 500,000 verified doctors across nine markets including Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam, Singapore and Taiwan. Its flagship product, Dx, is an AI clinical thinking partner that bundles clinical search and decision support, accredited continuing medical education, peer community and case discussion, and patient-ready summary notes into an invite-only mobile and web platform gated behind medical-credential verification. For life-sciences and enterprise partners Docquity sells an Intelligence Suite comprising Pulse, which measures healthcare-professional conviction and engagement, and Dialog, which runs field engagement and activation programs against that audience. Docquity also operates Docquity Jobs, a medical recruitment board. The company publishes no public API, developer portal or machine-readable specification; its api.docquity.com backend and id.docquity.com identity service exist to serve its own first-party applications and are not offered to third-party developers.

providers.name: Gaia
providers.description: Gaia (Gaia Family) is a value-based family-building company that makes fertility treatment financially accessible. Founded by Nader AlSalim after his own multi-year IVF journey, Gaia replaces unpredictable cycle-by-cycle IVF billing with fixed-price, all-inclusive plans and monthly payments, backed by a protection model that offers more tries — or money back — if treatment does not succeed. It partners with 180+ fertility clinics across the US and UK, covering IVF, egg freezing, embryo transfer, hormone and lab testing, and fertility navigation, and also offers fertility benefits to employers. This profile is a company lead (no public API surface) maintained in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Rupa Health
providers.description: Rupa Health (now a Fullscript company) is a healthcare platform that lets functional and root-cause medicine practitioners order, track, and receive results from specialty and functional lab tests across hundreds of lab companies through a single unified dashboard. It provides a lab test catalog, patient result portals, practitioner ordering and billing, phlebotomy coordination, and educational resources (Rupa University, the Root Cause Medicine podcast, and a lab reference guide). Rupa integrates with a range of EHR/EMR systems used by independent practitioners but does not publish a public developer API or developer portal at this time. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and Union Square Ventures.

providers.name: Scrutiny
providers.description: Scrutiny Global provides a market research and intelligence platform offering quantitative and qualitative survey programming, online panels, and API integration for B2B and healthcare sectors. Their services include CAWI, CATI, API-driven data collection, and compliance with ISO standards, serving global markets across Americas, EMEA, APAC, and MEA.

providers.name: Sevaro
providers.description: Sevaro (Sevaro Health) is a physician-led virtual neurology company that delivers telestroke, teleneurohospitalist rounding, remote EEG, neuro-intensive care, neuro-rehab and ambulatory neurology clinic services to hospitals across the United States. Its clinical delivery runs on Synapse AI, an integrated telemedicine platform that unifies EMR access, imaging, video, automated urgent call routing (Sevaro OneCall), AI stroke triage, ambient documentation and analytics, with companion Sevaro Video, Synapse for Providers, Synapse Analytics and Triage by Sevaro mobile surfaces. Sevaro sells to hospital systems through a demo-and-contract motion; it publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable API contract of any kind.

providers.name: Sofia
providers.description: Sofía is a 100% Mexican digital health insurance company that modernizes traditional medical coverage for enterprises, individuals, and families. Its plans combine zero-deductible major and minor medical care, preventive care with an assigned primary-care physician, and unlimited no-cost video consultations, all managed through a mobile app and an HR administrative portal. Sofía operates its own integrated medical network (SofíaMed) of hospitals and specialists, offers add-ons such as maternity, mental health, dental, and international coverage, and reimburses claims in an average of five business days. Backed by Ribbit Capital, Sofía positions insurance as a digital-first, member-centric health experience rather than a paper policy.

providers.name: Sprinter Health
providers.description: Sprinter Health is an in-home preventive and diagnostic healthcare company that pairs trained community health workers ("Sprinters") who visit patients at home with a virtual team of physicians, nurses, and care navigators. Its hybrid Sprinter Care+ model delivers vitals, blood draws, ECGs, cancer and diabetic screenings, wellness visits, medication reconciliation, care-gap closure, health risk assessments, and social-needs screening, and partners with health plans such as Humana, Molina Healthcare, and Anthem. Backed by a16z, Accel, General Catalyst, and GV. No public developer or API surface was found during enrichment; this profile captures the company's identity, security posture, and legal/trust properties.

providers.name: Brightline
providers.description: Brightline is an award-winning pediatric mental health practice delivering therapy, psychiatry (including medication management), and psychological testing for children and adolescents up to age 18, using an evidence-based, family-focused model that begins with a structured diagnostic evaluation. It treats anxiety, OCD, ADHD, disruptive behavioral disorders, depression, trauma, grief, and autism-spectrum symptoms via in-person clinics in New York and telehealth across NY, NJ, CT, MA, and WA, and operates BrightLife Kids, a free California state-funded behavioral health program for families with children up to age 12. Surfaced as a portfolio company of GV and Threshold Ventures; Brightline is a consumer/clinical healthcare provider with no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: LifeSite
providers.description: LifeSite is a data protection and digital asset company that helps organizations safeguard sensitive information, simplify compliance, and digitally verify ownership. Its Vault product is an encrypted store for personally identifiable, financial, and health information used by both enterprises and families to organize and collaborate on vital documents. TokenX, its Web3 arm, tokenizes real-world assets — critical minerals, carbon credits, and sports and consumer goods — so provenance and ownership can be authenticated without blockchain expertise. A Wellness product covers health, testing, and vaccination tracking for enterprises and events, and a Platform offering exposes LifeSite's building blocks and APIs for partners building tailored data-management applications. LifeSite is sales-led: the Platform APIs are described publicly but no developer portal, API reference, or specification is published, and access is arranged through a demo request.

providers.name: Novoic
providers.description: Novoic is a London-based clinical AI company building speech biomarkers for the early detection of Alzheimer's disease and cognitive impairment. Its technology analyzes how people speak - acoustic and linguistic patterns - to screen for subtle cognitive change in about ten minutes on any smart device. Products include Storyteller (automated, browser-based speech-based cognitive testing), Dashboard (an enterprise platform for running screening programs across sites with AI-assisted triage and analytics), and a Speech API for direct access to their speech processing, automated speech recognition, quality control, and speech-biomarker models. Novoic is deployed across 50+ medical institutions, partners with the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative, and emphasizes HIPAA/GDPR compliance. It also publishes two open-source feature-extraction libraries, surfboard (audio) and blabla (linguistics).

providers.name: UptimeHealth
providers.description: UptimeHealth is a healthcare operations platform for managing medical equipment service, compliance documentation, and facility maintenance across dental, medical, and veterinary practices from a single dashboard. The platform tracks devices, automates compliance tasks and logs, and coordinates repair service requests, reporting 73,000+ devices protected across 6,000+ facilities. UptimeHealth publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation — its platform (uptimecontroller.com) is a closed SaaS application.

providers.name: Aidence
providers.description: Aidence is a radiology AI company founded in Amsterdam in 2015 that builds clinical AI for the lung cancer pathway. Its flagship product, Veye Lung Nodules (now DeepHealth Lung), is a CE-marked AI solution that detects, classifies, quantifies, and measures growth of pulmonary nodules on chest CT scans, and is the AI of choice in NHS England's Targeted Lung Health Checks screening programme. Aidence was acquired by RadNet in 2022 and now operates under the DeepHealth brand; aidence.com redirects to deephealth.com/aidence. The product integrates with hospital systems over DICOM/PACS via the Veye Engine rather than a public developer REST API — no public API, developer portal, or SDKs are published. This profile captures the company's identity plus its probed security and disclosure posture.

providers.name: Almanac Health
providers.description: Almanac Health is a clinical AI company building a research-validated clinical decision support platform, delivered as Almanac Chat, that brings specialist-grade, evidence-based answers to clinicians at the point of care. Founded by physician-researcher Cyril Zakka, MD, the platform is designed to work within existing electronic health record (EHR) workflows, is governed by institutional controls, and is grounded in peer-reviewed research rather than pharmaceutical promotion. In April 2026 the company raised a $10 million seed round led by F-Prime with participation from General Catalyst and Lightspeed Venture Partners. This API Evangelist profile currently tracks the company's public web, trust, and security surface; Almanac Health does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: Cloudpost Networks
providers.description: CloudPost Networks is a Santa Clara, California device-security company founded in 2015 that rebranded as Ordr (ordr.net). It builds an AI-powered device intelligence and network-security platform that discovers, classifies, and secures connected devices across IT, IoT, OT, and IoMT environments, tying device identity to behavioral analytics so organizations can detect risk and automatically apply micro-segmentation and enforcement policies. Ordr serves 500+ healthcare, banking, and manufacturing organizations and integrates with vendors such as Cisco, Palo Alto Networks, CrowdStrike, and Fortinet. It maintains SOC 2 Type 2 compliance. No public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal is published.

providers.name: Walgreens Boots Alliance
providers.description: Walgreens Boots Alliance (WBA) is a global pharmacy-led health and wellbeing enterprise operating in more than 25 countries, with pharmacy chains Walgreens in the US and Boots in the UK, pharmaceutical wholesale and distribution through Alliance Healthcare, and specialty pharmacy operations. WBA operates as a Fortune 100 company and global healthcare platform, leveraging data science, AI, and digital health technologies to serve patients, customers, and health systems. While WBA's primary developer APIs are offered through the Walgreens Developer Program, the enterprise also uses healthcare data platforms for population health management, specialty pharmacy integration, and digital health services.

providers.name: BrightInsight
providers.description: BrightInsight is a regulated digital health platform for biopharma and medtech. Its cloud-based, microservices platform captures, transmits and analyzes data from CE-marked and FDA-regulated medical devices, combination products, apps and Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) in compliance with global security, privacy and regulatory requirements. The platform integrates with 400+ medical devices across 50+ manufacturers, connects to EHRs in 500+ U.S. provider networks, and is available in 48 countries. Founded in 2017 (formerly Flex Digital Health) and based in Alviso, California, BrightInsight is used by top biopharma and medtech companies to build and launch commercial regulated digital health solutions. It is a sales-led enterprise platform with no public developer portal or public API; integration is delivered under managed engagements.

providers.name: voize
providers.description: voize is a German healthcare AI company (voize GmbH) building a voice-documentation platform for long-term care, skilled nursing, and disability-support facilities. Caregivers speak naturally on a smartphone during patient care and voize's on-device and cloud speech models convert the free speech into structured, categorized entries that sync bi-directionally in real time into the facility's electronic health record (EHR) system. The product reduces documentation burden for nursing staff, works offline, recognizes patient names and corrects grammar, and integrates directly with major EHRs used in skilled nursing. voize is backed by HV Capital and operates in Germany and the United States. It ships a mobile application rather than a public developer API, but exposes EHR integrations, a trust center, and a vulnerability disclosure / bug bounty program on its public surface.

providers.name: Actym Therapeutics
providers.description: Actym Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing bacterial immunotherapies for solid tumors and fibrotic disease. Its STACT platform engineers an attenuated Salmonella typhimurium vehicle to be administered systemically and to deliver multiple therapeutic payloads that are amplified and produced locally at the disease site, with the goal of raising efficacy while limiting systemic toxicity. Its lead asset, ACTM-838, is in a Phase 1a/1b trial in patients with advanced solid tumors. Actym publishes no developer program, no API and no machine-readable contract; the only agent-facing surfaces on its own domain are a platform-generated llms.txt and an anonymous Wix Site MCP endpoint.

providers.name: ProcessBolt
providers.description: ProcessBolt, now operating as Perimeter, provides a painless Vendor Risk Management (VRM) platform for regulated industries. The solution offers continuous monitoring, automated assessments, AI‑powered document extraction, and real‑time risk scoring to help organizations reduce manual effort, improve vendor oversight, and meet compliance requirements. Backed by Techstars, Perimeter serves healthcare, finance, and enterprise customers with a cloud‑native, scalable service.

providers.name: AdaptX
providers.description: AdaptX is a Seattle-based clinical performance management company (founded 2016 as MDMetrix, renamed AdaptX in 2021) whose self-serve platform reads a hospital's existing electronic medical record data and turns it into near-real-time analytics that clinical, quality, operational and finance leaders use to measure and reduce clinical variation. Customers include Seattle Children's, Memorial Hermann, Children's Minnesota, USA Health and Kittitas Valley Healthcare, with published case studies covering surgical capacity, emergency department time-to-triage, length of stay, anesthetic greenhouse-gas reduction and health-equity stratification. The product is delivered as a hosted SaaS application on AWS to contracted health systems; as of this profiling pass AdaptX publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable API description.

providers.name: Aledade
providers.description: Aledade is a physician-led public benefit corporation and national leader in value-based care, partnering with independent primary care practices, community health centers, and health systems. It pairs data analytics, guided clinical workflows, integrated care solutions, and payer contracts to help primary care organizations succeed in accountable care organizations (ACOs) and value-based payment models, improving patient outcomes while supporting the business sustainability of independent practices.
